ei.title: It's Okay If Your Plans Don't Come True
ei.subject: 9월_2026 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: It's Okay If Your Plans Don't Come True

fullPassage: Letting go of our need for control, being aware, is a lot about gathering the courage to face uncertainty. Human beings want to know. When we don’t know, when things are uncertain, we often feel frightened and become inflexible. So we pretend that things are more predictable than they really are, even though we actually live with enormous uncertainty all the time. We cling to our plans and ideas about how things should be and turn out ever so desperately. And there’s nothing wrong with having plans. I think it’s a beautiful thing. But there’s a difference between planning and thinking all your plans have to come to fruition. American president Eisenhower once said: ‘Plans are worthless, but planning is everything.’ Imagine if we all used pencil instead of ink to write in our calendars and planners. Both figuratively and literally. Imagine if we could bear in mind that what we write down, what we think is going to happen, might not be what actually happens. And if we could try our best to be all right with that.

det.korean: ② rarely(좀처럼 ~않는) → actually(실제로): '늘(all the time)' 불확실성 속에 산다는 맥락이므로 실제로가 적절.

det.korean: 적은 것이 실제와 다를 수 있음을 받아들이자는 맥락 → 지웠다 고쳐 쓸 수 있는 '잉크 대신 연필'.

questions.passage: Letting go of our need for control, ①<u>being</u> aware, is a lot about gathering the courage to face uncertainty. Human beings want to know. When we don’t know, when things are ②<u>uncertain</u>, we often feel frightened and become inflexible. So we pretend that things are more predictable than they really are, even though we actually live with enormous uncertainty all the time. We cling to our plans and ideas about how things should be and turn out ever so desperately. And there’s nothing wrong with having plans. I think it’s a beautiful thing. But there’s a difference between planning and thinking all your plans have to ③<u>coming</u> to fruition. American president Eisenhower once said: ‘Plans are worthless, but planning is everything.’ Imagine if we all used pencil instead of ink to write in our calendars and planners. Both figuratively and literally. Imagine if we could bear in mind that what we write down, what we think is going to ④<u>happen</u>, might not be what actually happens. And if we could try our best to be all right with that.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 곳을 고르시오.

det.korean: ③ coming → come: 'all your plans have to ___ to fruition'에서 have to 뒤에는 동사원형 come이 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① being: 'control, being aware'의 분사구문(~한 채로), 정상
✅ ② uncertain: 'when things are uncertain'에서 be동사의 형용사 보어, 정상
❌ ③ coming: 'have to' 뒤에는 동사원형 come 필요 ←정답
✅ ④ happen: 'what we think is going to happen'에서 be going to + 동사원형, 정상
det.tip: have to + 동사원형. have to come to fruition (O), have to coming (X)
